utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the Case Number IT-03-69-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Will both parties make their appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution Dermot Groome assisted by Skye Winner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Geert-Jan Knoops and Mr. Wayne Jordash for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, lawyer Zoran Jovanovic. I'm Defence counsel for the accused Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. This is the first Status Conference, the last one being the one that was held at the same time at the provisional release hearing. And there are several pending matters in front of the Chamber that are currently being reviewed by the Chamber. Two motions of which is related to the protective measures which is sought by the Prosecution. That decision will be rendered in due course. And another matter which is related to some financial matters on the part of the Defence which has nothing to do with the Prosecution is also looked into by the Trial Chamber. I think that's all for the pending motions. Is there anything to raise from the parties in relation to pending motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I respectfully draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the fact that the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Trial Chamber III -- oh yes, II, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: II, oh yes, II. I respectfully draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the fact that the Defence in the case of Mr. Stanisic files a request to the Chamber to ask for an extension of time to file a reply to the registry's response in the remuneration case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are aware of the motion, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At yesterday's conference with respect to 65 ter, the Defence counsel of the accused Mr. Franko Simatovic joined in that request putting in a new motion which will be the subject of your decision making following a motion from the Prosecution. We still haven't received that material that the Prosecution has termed a sensitive sources. So we would like that deadline to be extended as well for us to be able to deal with that part of the disclosed material once it is disclosed and then we can conduct an investigation therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, you are referring to the pre-trial brief?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll come to that matter later. Well, why don't we deal with it directly. There's a request from Mr. Stanisic's Defence that -- for the extension of time in filing the Defence's pre-trial brief up until the 1st of March. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: It is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution has been filed -- was filed in July -- on 15th --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the 19th of July, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the Defence was given about four months from then. And there are still about -- almost two months from now up until 15th of November. Is it not a bit too early to speak about the extension at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you for this question, Your Honour. Maybe. The Defence is aware that the request was filed early. But on the other hand, as things look now we expect that we will not be able to comply with the time limit Your Honour sets due to, firstly, our own investigations which shed new light on certain new issues and certain other issues which are raised in the pre-trial brief extension motion. And on the other hand, we also draw the attention to the fact that we would not like to pose the Trial Chamber nor the Prosecution with a request for an extension of time limit very shortly before the limit expires which Your Honour has set. And with all due respect, I think it's a fair estimation the Defence has elaborated on in the motion itself. So we also think it's a matter of due diligence to already request for it now and not confront Your Honours and the Prosecutor with a request shortly before the time limit expires. Also in view of the fact that Your Honour may be thinking of scheduling at some moment the trial itself. So with all due respect, we don't think that the request is made too early before the time limit. And we reviewed the materials of the Prosecutor in the pre-trial brief and as Your Honours have noticed the pre-trial brief expands twice the normal size, so that means quite a task lies ahead of us. And, which you already see in our motion, it's the intention of the Defence in the case of Mr. Stanisic to file as much as possible a complete pre-trial brief where we intend to address all the issues. That's also one of the reasons that we seek more time than initially estimated by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Knoops. And I understand, as was put by Mr. Jovanovic, Mr. Simatovic's Defence team is joining in the same request of -- for an extension of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, I wanted to address that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Considering that I was sort of lenient in allowing extension of time on the part of the Prosecution the previous time and that some materials have yet to be disclosed -- but before that, Mr. Groome, do you have anything to say in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was my intention to respond in writing to the Defence motion. I'd still appreciate an opportunity to do that. Since there is no definite trial date, the Prosecution would have no objection of the Court using its discretion to manage when the brief is done. But I would add that I think that once the Prosecution is in possession of at least a provisional Defence trial brief, the sooner we have that, the sooner we can begin the process of identifying which issues really aren't at issue in the trial and we can begin to narrow the scope of the trial. So I think there is great benefit into -- at least having -- at least a provisional trial brief before us on schedule or soon thereafter so we can begin that process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Considering the two points I mentioned earlier, I'm minded to allow some extension of time, not in full as requested. I'm minded to give one more week after the winter recess. That will be until the 18th of January, which means the Defence team has been given about six months from the date the Prosecution's pre-trial brief was filed. I think that would be enough. So if you could do your best to comply with that deadline.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour, for your appreciation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will deal with some disclosure matters briefly. I understand that Rule 66 disclosure are almost complete, with the exception of those witnesses for whom the protective measures are being sought. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is correct with one exception. It was discovered this morning that a witness statement for a B179 was -- fell through the cracks as it were because the witness was reclassified from a sensitive source to a nonsensitive source at the last minute. That has been disclosed to both counsel today. So at this stage now they are in possession of all the witness statements that we are obliged to turn over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And also I was informed that there are four witness statements where translations are outstanding together with two audiotapes and the interviews of Mr. Todorovic and Vasiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We anticipate that we will have those translations and those audiotapes duplicated in the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I ask: did Mr. Vasiljkovic appear in another trial didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But at that time the B/C/S version was not disclosed. What was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, they have the English -- the English transcript of all of that was disclosed. I believe it was a problem in the duplication of the audio/videotape so that they had -- that the Defence is in possession of a B/C/S version of prior statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. And in relation to exhibits, most of them are also disclosed with some exceptions, which will be disclosed in due course, very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Predominantly all the exhibits have been disclosed. Ms. Winner is in the process of doing an audit to be sure that all translations -- that there were no mistakes made. But at this stage all the exhibits have been disclosed on a single DVD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, there are translations of 215 autopsy reports which are outstanding and they are remaining a low priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Given the workload that CLSS is now facing, these autopsy reports are mostly comprised of just names of the person, when they went missing and different material that -- it's actually easy to understand what the document says without being translated. And I think of all the documents or all the translations that we are endeavouring to complete, that it would be of the lowest priority of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has five expert witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the reports -- four reports of whom are disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage the reports of four of those experts now have been disclosed or filed. In yesterday's 65 ter Conference I informed the senior legal officer that we intended to formally file the -- those reports of the four experts and it was agreed among the parties that in lieu of that that it would be understood that our disclosure would place Defence counsel on notice and they have in fact filed their response to those expert reports. There was one outstanding addendum to Mr. Nielsen's report that was filed yesterday. So now all four of the experts -- all of their work is before the Chamber. The only outstanding one is Ms. Ewa Tabeau, which she is currently fully engaged in completing reports for other cases that have definite trial dates and some even have trial dates early in the new year. I've spoken with her, she believes that she can complete her work in this case prior to the Christmas break. For the most part her work will be simply a subset of the report which she filed in the Milosevic case, which has been disclosed to counsel. There are some new statistics from Croatia which she will be supplementing and creating an addendum. So there will be some different material but predominantly it is the exact same material and her findings are exactly the same as the report already in the possession of counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that the Defence is to file their pre-trial brief by 18th of January, is it not possible for her to shorten the preparation time for her report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've discussed this with her. I mean, I think part of the problem that the Office of the Prosecutor is now facing is that many people are leaving and with a hiring freeze we are unable to hire people to replace them. Especially with somebody whose expertise in this particular field -- I can always ask her to do her best to complete the work as soon as possible. She works very hard, and I know she will do that. But it is a matter of cases -- that she is under very strict deadlines so that they can begin the trials in January. But of course I will convey the Court's wish that it be done sooner than December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is suggested by the Prosecution is the basic structure and the main content will be remaining the same as the one which was tendered in Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Exactly the same. As I explained to Defence counsel yesterday, if they simply draw a line through those municipalities which are not part of this indictment, they will virtually have the exact -- they will have the final report but it will have a different caption on it. And then the additional piece which is what she needs to work on is just the information -- it's new information that's available about internally displaced persons from Croatia which was not part of the Milosevic report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard that, what would you say that if I put a deadline on Dr. Tabeau's report as 15th of December so that the Defence will work on the pre-existing draft and then have one month to edit anything if anything appears on the new report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We would be grateful for that, Your Honour, and perhaps it would assist counsel if as soon as she has a draft of that report I will forward that so they can begin their work and they will have some preview of what her final report will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any say, Mr. Knoops or Jovanovic, on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And there are some several supporting materials to be disclosed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are some supporting materials for the disclosure of the expert reports which we are putting together and will forward to Defence counsel as soon as possible. Mr. Nielsen's first report, 80 per cent of the material has now been disclosed. We will disclose the remainder on EDS -- on the electronic disclosure system as soon as it is available and Mr. Nielsen's addendum to his report we are currently having translations made of those documents. And as soon as they are received we will forward them. Ms. Tabeau, there is an addendum to -- that was provided because she is a witness provided -- regarding her work on the Galic trial. Although we were legally obliged to disclose that, it really has no relevance for this case. If Defence counsel are able to indicate to us which, if any, of the source material that the experts rely on is of greater interest to them, we can of course shift the priority so that material gets translated -- and to them first. So it would be of assistance to us to know which reports or which material upon which those reports were based is of the greatest assistance to them in preparing their pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Defence must have heard that. In relation to pre-trial brief, Prosecution suggested they are minded to use the Rule 92 bis in the presentation of their evidence. How many of them, could you remind them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Essentially the Prosecution will endeavour to use Rule 92 bis or 89(F) wherever it is possible. So in the Prosecution pre-trial brief we had proposed that 11 witnesses be taken completely viva voce, that 49 witnesses be taken completely under Rule 92 bis, and that 55 witnesses be taken partially under 92 bis or 89(F). That would be a total of 120 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. But the parties didn't find the time to discuss about the matter or 92 bis or agreed or adjudicated facts yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would encourage you to find the time, suitable time, to discuss it. In relation to experts on any other matters, there will be -- there are many witnesses which will be related to both of the accused. So I wonder whether the Trial Chamber could expect some kind of coordinations between the Defence team of the two accused, for example in certain cross-examination which Defence to go first or whether is there be some common factual base. So I would encourage that, but before trial begins, even in pre-trial cases, in submitting pre-trial briefs there may be some common grounds which is common to both of the accused. So can I expect that such coordination between the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as the Defence of Mr. Stanisic concerns, there is no reason to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order to avoid some repetition and also concentrate on more specific, important issues. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Of course, we're willing to share our ideas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any other matters to be dealt with today? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one matter with respect to Rule 68 material which I feel obliged to bring to your attention. Much of the Rule 68 material now will be placed in the electronic disclosure system. As of today, approximately 50 per cent of the material that will be placed in that system is there now and is searchable by Defence counsel. It will be another six weeks, perhaps a little bit longer, before 100 per cent of the search material will be in that system. So until that time, as Defence counsel don't have full access to the collections or the searchable collections of the Office of the Prosecutor and I wanted to bring that to your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you're confident that it will be completed in six weeks time from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have very little confidence in any deadline, Your Honour, given that the dire circumstances under which we find ourselves these days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No observation from the Defence on that matter. Any matters to raise from the Defence. Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The Defence is already selecting the material that it can access on the Prosecution's side. So that's what we're doing at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just go back very briefly to the issue of the Rule 68 material just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- just to raise the issue now that clearly what goes into our pre-trial brief may be subject to what we find within the Rule 68 material. There is a huge amount which needs to be gone through. So simply just to flag up that what is in that pre-trial brief, lest it will be our Defence in some detail, will obviously be subject to what is or may be discovered within the overall Rule 68 material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. We shall see what will come up later. Mr. Stanisic, is there anything you would like to raise now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED STANISIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SIMATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So I officially put on record that the Prosecution's expert reports, four of them, are filed officially, and the Defence responded that they are going to -- that they wish to cross-examine all of them. And I think that concludes the Status Conference for today. And I was informed that the next Status Conference, the deadline for it is the 21st of January next year. I am going to have it on Thursday, 20th of January, if the courtroom is available, but I will let you know. That is the time that we got in our hand the brief from the Defence. The hearing is adjourned. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 3.29 p.m.
